html:
A battle fought in June 530 outside the Roman frontier fortress of Dara, in what is now southeast Turkey, in which the young general Belisarius beat a larger Persian army.

It came during the Iberian War between Justinian and the Persian shah Kavad I. Belisarius dug a line of trenches in front of the walls with gaps for counter attacks, put his weak infantry behind them, and kept cavalry, including Hunnic horsemen, on the flanks. When the Persian attacks bent his left wing, a hidden band of Heruli horsemen struck the Persians from behind a hill and they broke.

The historian Procopius, Belisarius's secretary, was there and described it. It was one of the few big Roman field wins over Persia in this era, and it made Belisarius's name before his wars in Africa and Italy. The Persians won the next year at Callinicum, and the war ended with the Perpetual Peace of 532.
sum: A battle fought in June 530 outside the Roman frontier fortress of Dara, in what is now southeast Turkey, in which the young general Belisarius beat a larger Persian army.
